title: Patient portal API latency runbook
content: Service: patient-portal-api on Cloud Run. SLO: p95 latency under 800 ms. 1. Compare p95 latency, request rate and 5xx rate for the last 60 minutes. 2. Check whether a new revision was deployed in the last 2 hours. If latency rose right after, roll traffic back to the previous revision. 3. Check cold starts: if instance count drops to zero overnight, set min-instances to 1 for business hours. 4. Check Cloud SQL connections. If active connections exceed 80 percent of the limit, scale the connection pool before adding instances. 5. Inspect traces for slow spans, usually the appointment-search query or the identity provider call. Escalate to Sev2 if p95 stays above 2 seconds for 15 minutes.

title: FHIR gateway CrashLoopBackOff runbook
content: Service: fhir-gateway on GKE namespace clinical-api. 1. Run kubectl describe pod and read the Events section for probe failures, image pull errors or OOMKilled. 2. Read logs from the previous container with kubectl logs --previous. 3. A missing or rotated secret for the EHR vendor API key is the most common cause after a key rotation. 4. If the pod is OOMKilled, compare memory usage with the limit of 1 GiB and raise the limit one step at a time. 5. If the liveness probe fails during startup, increase initialDelaySeconds before changing application code. Never paste patient identifiers into tickets or chat while debugging.

title: E-prescribing service elevated 5xx runbook
content: Service: eprescribing-svc on Cloud Run. It calls the fictional partner network RxLink. 1. Split 5xx errors by upstream: our code, RxLink timeouts, or database errors. 2. If RxLink timeouts dominate, check the partner status page and enable the retry queue with a maximum of 3 retries. 3. Do not drop prescriptions. Failed submissions must stay in the dead-letter topic until a pharmacist reviews them. 4. If the error rate exceeds 5 percent for 10 minutes, declare Sev2 and notify the clinical operations lead.

title: Lab results Pub/Sub backlog runbook
content: Service: lab-results-worker on GKE, subscription lab-results-sub. 1. Check oldest unacked message age. Target: under 5 minutes. 2. If the backlog grows while workers are healthy, scale the deployment and check the horizontal pod autoscaler metrics. 3. If many messages are redelivered, look for a poison message that fails parsing and move it to the dead-letter topic. 4. Confirm downstream FHIR writes succeed before replaying messages, to avoid duplicate lab results in patient charts.

title: PHI in logs and telemetry policy
content: Logs, traces and metrics must never contain patient names, dates of birth, medical record numbers or free-text clinical notes. Use opaque internal IDs only. Telemetry attributes are reviewed in code review. If PHI is found in logs: 1) declare a security incident, 2) restrict access to the affected log bucket, 3) notify the privacy officer within 24 hours, 4) fix the code path, 5) purge affected entries under the privacy officer's guidance.

title: Incident severity and escalation
content: Sev1: patient-facing outage or possible PHI exposure. Page primary on-call and incident commander immediately. Update every 15 minutes. Sev2: major feature degraded, such as e-prescribing or lab results. Page primary on-call. Update every 30 minutes. Sev3: minor degradation with a workaround. Ticket during business hours. Primary on-call escalates to secondary after 10 minutes without acknowledgement. A postmortem is required for Sev1 and Sev2 within 5 business days.

title: Postmortem: claims-engine outage (fictional, Sev2)
content: Summary: claims submissions failed for 47 minutes after a config change. Impact: about 3,200 claims delayed, no data lost. Root cause: a new batch-size setting of 5000 exhausted memory, causing repeated OOM kills in claims-engine. Detection: queue age alert fired after 12 minutes. Latency alerts did not fire because requests never completed. Fix: reverted the setting and added a memory-based alert. Actions: add config validation in CI, add a canary rollout for claims-engine, add a dashboard for queue age.

title: Aurelius service level objectives
content: patient-portal-api: availability 99.9 percent monthly, p95 latency under 800 ms. eprescribing-svc: availability 99.95 percent, successful submission rate above 99.5 percent. lab-results-worker: oldest message age under 5 minutes for 99 percent of the time. When the monthly error budget is more than 75 percent used, freeze non-critical deploys until the budget recovers.
